claims.proof_source: per T the real unit vector (a_T,b_T)/sqrt(q_i(T)) has computational-basis law (1-theta_T,theta_T) and Hadamard-basis law (u_T,1-u_T), u_T=(a_T+b_T)^2/(2q_i(T)); Maassen-Uffink (PRL 60 (1988) 1103) for two mutually unbiased qubit bases gives h2(theta_T)+h2(u_T)>=1; J_i=sum_T q_i(T)(1-h2(u_T)) and B_i=sum_T q_i(T)h2(theta_T)
proof_dependencies: Maassen-Uffink entropic uncertainty relation (external, cited from memory)

claims.exact_statement: For every f and every finite fair adaptive stopping tree with stopped function g_tau: H(f)-E H(g_tau)-(3/ln 2)[I(f)-E I(g_tau)] <= E sum_{t<tau} lambda_t <= H(f)-E H(g_tau). For complete trees H(f)-(3/ln 2)I(f) <= E sum lambda_t <= H(f). Consequently FEI holds iff some (equivalently every) complete tree has E sum lambda_t <= K I(f) for an absolute K, with constants differing by at most 3/ln 2.

claims.exact_statement: Let C* be the best FEI constant (possibly infinite), K* = sup over nonconstant g of min_{i: d_i>0} D_i/d_i, and K*_lambda the same with lambda_i. Then C* <= K* <= C* + min(2/ln 2, C*) and C* - 3/ln 2 <= K*_lambda <= C*. Pointwise for nonconstant g: min_i D_i/d_i <= H/I + min(2/ln 2, H/I) and min_i lambda_i/d_i <= (sum_i B_i)/I <= H/I. Equivalently, FEI holds iff there is an absolute K such that every f has a coordinate i with KL(nu_i||q_i) >= log2(1/Inf_i(f)) - K.

claims.first_unproved_line: Every Boolean function has a coordinate i with D_i <= K Inf_i for an absolute K (equivalently KL(nu_i||q_i) >= log2(1/Inf_i) - K). This is FEI itself up to 2/ln 2 and is unproved.

claims.exact_statement: For every complete tree and every coordinate rule, E sum_t (D_t - C d_t) = H(f) - C I(f); for a stopping tree it equals (H(f)-C I(f)) - E[H(g_tau) - C I(g_tau)]. The minimal nonnegative potential Q*_v = max(0, D_v - C d_v + avg Q*_children) (Q*=0 at leaves) satisfies D_t <= C d_t + Q_t - E[Q_{t+1}|F_t], is dominated by every nonnegative potential with that property, and gives H(f) <= C I(f) + Q*_root; Q*_root = 0 under the greedy D/d rule whenever C >= K*. Hence positive expected whole-path debt on a complete tree is exactly a counterexample to H <= C I, independent of the rule, and stopping-rule falsifiers can only target Q*.
